# Unit tests for next-step classification and renderer normalisation

## Goal / use case

Test-first coverage for parent AC2, AC3 and AC4: the shared
routine-next-step classifier in `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` and the report
renderer's producer-actions normalisation in
`skill/report/scripts/render_report.py`, written before the implementations
land (F1/F2).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `skill/shared/tests/test_herdr_pane.py` covers the classifier:
  "Proceed to /skill:plan", "Review the intake brief and then run
  /skill:plan" and "Next step: implement" classify as routine; "None
  needed" is unchanged; ambiguous/text-with-blocking-clauses falls back
  unchanged (all-clauses-must-match).
- AC2: `derive_status` returns "done" (not ⚠️ `note`) when all ACs are
  met and producer actions contain only routine next-step progression.
- AC3: `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` asserts the rendered
  "## Producer Actions" section reads exactly "None needed" for
  routine-only text, and that the renderer emits a single stderr diagnostic
  naming the discarded text.
- AC4: Regression tests assert genuine blocking actions ("Answer the OPEN
  QUESTION in comment SA-C… before /skill:plan can start", "Approve the
  remediation list in comment #4") are rendered unchanged (no over-eager
  stripping).
- AC5: Tests are written first and each asserts current-code behaviour it
  targets (documenting which cases pass/fail until F1/F2 land).

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/tests/test_herdr_pane.py`
- `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py`
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py`
- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py`
data.title: Unit tests for next-step classification and renderer normalisation

# Baseline regression tests for full-suite resolution (test-first)

## Goal

Pin today's suite-resolution behaviour **before** the hidden skill-test rule
lands, so the "zero candidates → byte-identical" and "changed-scope
untouched" guarantees of SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB are enforced by durable green
tests — not only by inspection. This is the test-first slice of the parent:
it is written and committed green first; the behaviour changes in later
children must keep it green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Byte-identity baseline.** A parameterised test asserts
  `full_suite_commands(tmp_path)` equals the current resolved set for: a
  pytest-only repo, a pytest+node repo, an npm-only repo, and a repo with a
  pinned `suiteCommands` list; each result contains no command referencing
  `.pi/skills`.
- **AC2 — No-`.pi/skills` repo stays identical.** A test asserts a repo with
  NO `.pi/skills/*/tests` (the general case today, including the SorraAgents
  repo itself) resolves to the exact same command set once the F1 rule lands
  — the assertion is written against the F0 baseline and remains green after
  F1–F3 (enforced by the full suite).
- **AC3 — Changed-scope baseline.** `changed_scope_commands()` regression:
  for a representative changed file under `skill/test/`, the emitted subset
  command matches the current expectation and stays unchanged after F1–F3.
- **AC4 — Green at baseline.** The new tests pass via the test skill full
  suite before any resolver change is made.

## Key Files

- `skill/test/tests/test_suite_resolution.py` — extend the backward-compat
  class with the no-`.pi/skills` byte-identity assertions (AC1/AC2)
- `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py` — changed-scope baseline (AC3)
data.title: Baseline regression tests for full-suite resolution

data.description:
## Summary

The implement and intake skills claim work items by setting the assignee (the
agent identity) and `status=in_progress` at the start of their run. When the
run reaches ANY terminal outcome — success, failure, or abort — the assignee
is never cleared. Under the assignee-hold convention (AGENTS_GLOBAL: "non-empty
assignee = scheduling hold (producer `Map`; clear to release)") a lingering
assignee holds the item and blocks re-dispatch/re-pickup.

The audit skill already clears the assignee on terminal verdicts
(SA-0MV98PAT7005VXXS); implement and intake must mirror that behaviour:
every terminal outcome clears the assignee so the item is released for the
producer and the next lifecycle step.

## User Story

As a dispatcher/producer, I need the implement and intake skills to clear the
assignee at the end of every run (success, failure, or abort) so completed or
released work items are never left on a scheduling hold.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — shared `StatusLifecycle` context manager
  (opt-in `clear_assignee_on_exit=True` clears the assignee on the successful
  `completed` transition; default `False` keeps other skills unchanged. The
  failure path still clears the assignee only when constructed with
  `assignee=`)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_start` (claim, failure
  resets), `phase_finish` (success via `StatusLifecycle` + failure resets),
  `phase_abort` (reset to `open`)
- `skill/intake/scripts/intake.py` — `cmd_start` (claim), `cmd_finish`,
  `cmd_auto_complete`, `cmd_abort`, failure resets
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md`, `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — document the
  clear-on-completion behaviour
- Tests: `skill/implement/tests/` (incl. `test_phase_abort_clears_assignee.py`,
  `test_finish_no_diff_status.py`, `test_phase_start_claim.py`),
  `skill/intake/tests/test_intake_scripts_cwd.py`,
  `skill/shared/test_status_lifecycle.py`, and the parent-advance assertions in
  `tests/test_implement_parent_recursion.py` / `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `implement.py finish` success path clears the assignee while still
      advancing status to `completed` / stage `in_review`
- [ ] Every `implement.py` failure reset (start/finish) and `phase_abort`
      clears the assignee together with the reset to `open`
- [ ] `intake.py finish`, `auto-complete`, and `abort` each clear the assignee
      (and failure resets do too)
- [ ] The shared `StatusLifecycle` supports opt-in clear-on-success so other
      skills are unaffected unless they request it (no silent behaviour change)
- [ ] Both `SKILL.md` files document that completion clears the assignee
      regardless of outcome
- [ ] Regression tests cover success and failure/abort outcomes for both
      skills; all tests pass
- [ ] Full project test suite passes at the dev-push gate

## Assumptions

- "Regardless of the state of the completion" = every terminal outcome
  (success → `in_review`, failure/abort → `open`) clears the assignee.
- Assignee clearing is applied only where the skill itself owns the
  transitional update (final `completed`/`open` writes), not to arbitrary
  comments or intermediate updates.
data.title: implement/intake: clear assignee on completion regardless of outcome
